t: The great southern kingdom of ancient China, based on the middle Yangtze and the Han River.
Its rulers called themselves kings from 704 BCE and absorbed dozens of states, organising many as counties.
Its distinctive culture produced the Songs of Chu, and Chu rebels overthrew the Qin dynasty that had conquered it.
dyk: The oldest known manuscript of parts of the Daodejing was found in a Chu tomb at Guodian, written on bamboo slips around 300 BCE.
ev: Xiong Tong proclaims himself king as King Wu of Chu
King Zhuang defeats Jin at the Battle of Bi
The State of Wu defeats Chu at Boju and occupies Ying
Nobles kill the reformer Wu Qi after the death of King Dao
Bai Qi of Qin captures Ying; the capital moves to Chen
Chu moves its capital to Shouchun
The Qin general Wang Jian captures King Fuchu and annexes Chu

f.capital: Danyang; Ying from c. 689 BCE; later Chen and Shouchun
